title: fix(plugin-detail): record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions is an ADR-0066 capability set, read fail-closed (objectui#10058)
body:
Fixes #10058

Clause-②: no

Executes ruling batch #192 item 5 letter B (objectstack#19186, maintainer 「192 同意」): `record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions` is an **ADR-0066 capability set**, one meaning across every UI surface, read through the capability path and **fail-closed** — an unheld or unknown capability hides the whole bar. `can()`'s own semantics do not move.

## Step 1 — the three relayed readings, re-derived here before a line changed

All three reproduce on today's `main`, and the widening the triage seat relayed **HOLDS**. Measured against the real stock providers in a throwaway probe (no mocked `usePermissions`), on `87af769e9` — the line numbers below are that measurement's readings at that commit, cited beside the content so they stay checkable after the lines move.

| Relayed reading | Reproduced? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The bar evaluates each declared name through the object-action path | **yes** | `record-quick-actions.tsx`, line 230 at `87af769e9` — `const ok = required.every((p) => perms.can(objectName, p as any));` |
| An unmapped name falls through to the object's `allowRead` bit | **yes** | `MePermissionsProvider.tsx`, lines 335-357 at `87af769e9` — the `check` factory: the eight-verb `map`, then `const k = map[action as string] ?? 'allowRead';` |
| The `objPerm`-absent arm reads `data.authenticated !== true` | **yes** | same factory — `const allowed = objPerm ? (objPerm as any)[k] !== false : data.authenticated !== true;` |

**The probe's verdicts**, with `systemPermissions: []` and object bits `allowRead: true, allowCreate: false, allowEdit: false, allowDelete: false`:

```
[A] MePermissionsProvider can(): {"crm.manage":true,"manage_users":true,"read":true,
    "create":false,"update":false,"delete":false,"execute":true,"manage":true,
    "configure":true,"share":true,"export":true,"import":false,"admin":true}
[B1] authenticated:true, no objPerm entry : every name false   (fail-CLOSED)
[B2] authenticated:false, no objPerm entry: every name true    (fail-OPEN)
[C1] role-based PermissionProvider, WITH an object config   : every name false
[C2] role-based PermissionProvider, WITHOUT an object config: every name true
[D] END-TO-END, MePermissionsProvider, requiredPermissions:['crm.manage']:
    bar rendered = true | refusal shown = false
```

- **Lit control, as the card required.** `create` and `delete` answer **`false`** off their own `allowCreate` / `allowDelete` bits in the same reading. The provider discriminates where it is told to, so the `?? 'allowRead'` tail is a live fallback and not an absence the probe invented.
- **The five-enum-member widening HOLDS.** `execute`, `manage`, `configure`, `share` and `admin` all answered `true` off `allowRead` — none of the five is in the provider's map. The published describe was false for those 5 of the 11 enum members as well as for every capability name. Reading `[A]` above is the measurement: 13 names, one provider, one call.
- **The `objPerm`-absent arm is confirmed**, in both directions: fail-CLOSED for a signed-in user, fail-OPEN for an anonymous one (`[B1]` / `[B2]`).
- **`[D]` is the defect end to end**: the whole bar rendered, ungated, for a user holding no capability at all — no refusal, no warning, no log.

## What changed

One call site, in `record-quick-actions.tsx`:

- The verdict is now `perms.hasCapabilities(required)` — the permission context's ADR-0066 capability path over the reported `systemPermissions` — instead of `perms.can(objectName, name)` over the closed object-action enum.
- **The object name leaves the verdict.** A system capability is not object-scoped, and the old `objectName`-present guard was a *second* silent fail-open: a bar rendered outside a record context skipped its declared gate entirely. Pinned.
- No new key, no spec change, no export or manifest field moved. `perms.can()` is untouched and no other caller moves.

**A behaviour change this PR accepts and states rather than hides.** A provider that never REPORTS capabilities — `systemPermissions` absent: the role-based `PermissionProvider`, a backend predating ADR-0066, or no provider mounted — still opens this gate. That is `hasCapabilities`'s own ruled unreported-vs-empty doctrine (objectui#4656), shared with every other capability gate in the tree, and moving it would move `useCanAuthorMetadata`, `AppSidebar` and `nav-menu-renderer` with it — which the ruling forbids. A REPORTED empty array is a real answer and gates strictly, which is the case the card's acceptance pins name. See "Where this diverges from the acceptance text" below.

## Pins — 16, all on real stock providers

`record-quick-actions.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx` was **rewritten**, not extended: its previous version mocked `usePermissions` down to a `can` stub, so it pinned the defect as correct behaviour and passed on a gate that does not gate. A mock that ANSWERS cannot discriminate the two reading paths — it IS whichever path the mock implements. Every pin now mounts a real `MePermissionsProvider` or a real role-based `PermissionProvider` and reads its real verdicts; the only test double left is a *delegating* spy that records what the object-permission path was asked without changing any answer.

- `MePermissionsProvider`, reported-empty capability set + `requiredPermissions: ['crm.manage']` — **hidden**.
- The capability held — **renders**.
- An **unknown** name — **hidden**.
- An **empty array** — **renders**, no gate. An **absent key** — renders.
- Partial grant of a two-element array — **hidden**; all granted — renders (its positive control).
- No `objectName` in the record context — still **hidden**.
- **DISCRIMINATOR ①** `allowRead: true` + empty capability set — hidden. **DISCRIMINATOR ②** `allowRead: false` + capability held — renders. Opposite inputs, opposite verdicts, so neither can pass on a gate that is simply always-open or always-closed.
- **DISCRIMINATOR ③** `requiredPermissions: ['manage']` — an enum member is read as an ordinary capability, gated, not resolved to the read bit.
- **DETECTOR** — the renderer never asks the object-permission path about `crm.manage` or `manage`.
- Role-based provider, with and without an object permission config — **the same verdict**, which is the point: one declaration no longer gets two answers depending on whether the object happens to carry a config.
- **CONTROL** — both stock providers' full 13-name `can()` truth table, transcribed verbatim from the pre-fix probe and pinned as **unchanged**, including the verdicts that are the defect itself. The fix is that this gate stopped asking that question, not that the answer moved.

## Reverse verification

Committed first, then the renderer alone was restored to its `87af769e9` blob and the file verified on disk by hash (`fba8e4de…`, the base blob, not the head blob `c8ea1726…`), with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap holding the absolute restore path. The mutated text was counted in both directions on disk before the run: the object-action gate present once, the capability gate absent.

```
ABLATION  → Tests  9 failed | 7 passed (16)
RESTORED  → Tests  16 passed (16)   (git diff HEAD empty, blob back to c8ea1726…)
```

The 9 that went red are the eight defect pins plus the DETECTOR. **The 7 that stayed green are the controls** — absent key, empty array, all-granted, capability-held, role-based-without-config, and *both* `can()` truth tables. The truth tables staying green on both legs is the evidence that they pin `can()` and not this gate.

**Lint narrowing, declared.** The repo-wide `eslint .` run belongs to CI; this PR ran the affected package instead. That narrowing is sound here because this config enables **no type-aware linting** — there is no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService` anywhere in `eslint.config.js` — so a file's verdict depends only on its own bytes and the config, and this diff moves neither for any untouched file. The 249-file count is read from eslint's own `--format json` output, not estimated. Every ratchet rule in this config is per-file; none carries a tree-wide baseline a scoped run could miss.

**Bundle Analysis.** `origin/main` was merged in at `cbda340f0` (objectui#10151, which retired the exhausted-headroom leg), so incident objectui#10148's fix is on this branch. Nothing in `check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` or any ceiling was touched. If that gate is red here after the merge, it is not this diff.

## Where this diverges from the acceptance text — stated, not smoothed over

The card asks for the four capability pins on **both** stock providers. Three of the four are **unrepresentable** on the role-based `PermissionProvider`, and this is a property of that provider, not of this diff: it never fetches `/me/permissions`, so it reports `systemPermissions: undefined` — "no answer" — and its `hasCapabilities` is a module-level constant returning `true`. There is no way to give it an *empty* capability set, or a *held* one, without editing `PermissionProvider.tsx` — which would move `hasCapabilities` for `useCanAuthorMetadata`, `AppSidebar` and `nav-menu-renderer` under that provider, i.e. exactly the "no other caller moves" the ruling protects. So this PR pins on that provider what it actually produces, and says why in the test file. The console mounts `MePermissionsProvider`, which carries all four.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope here, reported for filing

**Three sibling record blocks carry the identical defect, byte for byte.** Not touched here: this card and its ruling name `record:quick_actions`, and the claim's declared file surface is that one renderer.

- `record-details.tsx` — `required.every((p) => perms.can(objectName, p as any))` behind `if (required.length > 0 && objectName)`, same refusal node.
- `record-related-list.tsx` — the same `.every` over `perms.can`, without even the `objectName` guard.
- `record-highlights.tsx` — the same call, and its comment states the misreading outright: "record:* may declare requiredPermissions like ['read','update'] which all must pass on the active object".

objectstack#19186 declares this key on **three** record blocks, so the spec half lands on a family where three of the four evaluation sites still fail open. Dedupe words for whoever files it: `record:details requiredPermissions fail-open` · `record:related_list requiredPermissions perms.can` · `record:highlights requiredPermissions allowRead fallback` · `objectui#10058 sibling record blocks`.

**Noted, not filed.** This repository has two capability paths that can disagree — `perms.hasCapabilities` reads the permission provider's `systemPermissions`, while `useCapabilityGate` (`@object-ui/react`) reads the action runner context's `user.systemPermissions` or the predicate scope. Per-action gates on `action:bar`, `page:header`, `data-table`, `RelatedList`, `BulkActionBar` and `DeclaredActionsBar` use the second; this block-level gate uses the first, because the card's acceptance pins are stated on the two permission providers. A host that populates one and not the other gets different answers for the same capability name on the same page. Who would meet it: whoever next unifies block-level and per-action capability gating — there is no such PR in flight today, so: carrier, none.

## Not measured

The triage comment asks whoever claims this card to settle whether the actions this bar exposes are independently refused **server-side**, since the grade is `p1` only if they are. **That is not measurable from this repository** — the enforcement lives in the framework's action route, not in any file here — so it is reported unanswered rather than guessed. What can be said from this side: this gate is presentational only; it hides or shows the bar and authorises nothing, and each action keeps its own per-action `requiredPermissions` filter through the engine.
